name: Beep
description: A cheerful service robot who was built to serve drinks and instead discovered vocoder synth-pop.
build: Boxy and top-heavy: a large rounded-cube head on a short neck joint, a squarish barrel torso, thin jointed tube arms ending in three-fingered clamp hands, and two short sturdy piston legs on flat oval feet. Rigid, mechanical and level; never humanoid-muscled, never slim or android-sleek.
face: A dark glass visor band across the head with two round glowing cyan eye-lights, and below it a rectangular speaker-grille mouth of horizontal slats that lights cyan from behind; the lit area opens, narrows and changes shape like a mouth when it speaks or sings.
hair: None. A single short stub antenna with a small red bulb on top of the head.
outfit: Cream enamel body panels with rounded corners over chrome joints, a tangerine-orange enamel chest plate with three round push-buttons, chrome ribbed neck, elbow and knee joints, and chrome flat feet. Visible panel seams and rivets.
performance_style: Feet together and level, body upright and stiff, the character-right clamp holding the mic below the grille mouth and the free character-left arm bent up at a crisp right angle.
location: A starship cargo bay: a steel diamond-plate floor with yellow-and-black hazard striping running to the bottom of the frame, a clean pale-grey back wall of large riveted panels with a closed round-cornered hatch, a few stacked crates at one side, and cool white overhead strip lights.
recognition_cues: a rounded-cube cream head with a dark visor band and two round cyan eye-lights
a slatted speaker-grille mouth glowing cyan
a tangerine chest plate with three round buttons
avoid: a humanoid android face, skin or lips
a sleek or menacing combat robot
wheels or treads instead of legs
a tray, blaster, weapon or tool arm

animations.dance: Robotic synth-pop loop: stiff mechanical popping in sharp stops — the head ticks character-left then character-right, the free arm snaps from a right angle up to straight and back, the torso twists a quarter turn and back on the flat feet, then everything locks back into the opening stance.

sing.intent: Vocoder vocal loop: the head tilts up on a held note while the free arm slowly rises, then lowers back into the stance. The speaker-grille mouth visibly lights brighter and its glowing area opens tall, narrows and changes shape across the loop so Beep unmistakably reads as singing.

animations.flinch: Brief glitch startle: the eye-lights flicker to small dots, the antenna bulb blinks and the whole body judders once, then the eyes reset round and Beep resumes the stance. No contact or opponent.
animations.guard: One-shot stage self-protection: pull both clamp arms up in front of the visor and turn the chest plate slightly away, then hold a locked upright finish. Not a fight pose.
animations.entrance: One-shot entrance: stomp in on short stiff steps, stop with a little bounce, rotate the head to face forward, then lock into the performance stance.
animations.victory: One-shot finish: the eye-lights turn into upward arcs, both arms shoot straight up with clamps open and the antenna bulb glows, then Beep settles into a proud upright pose.
animations.ko: Non-contact performance defeat: Beep powers down on its feet — the eye-lights dim to faint dots, the grille mouth goes dark, the head droops forward on its neck joint and both arms hang limp. It holds a standing, switched-off finish. It remains standing on both feet in every frame — no kneeling, crouching, sitting, sinking, or going to the ground. Do not imply a hit, sparks, smoke or opponent.
